findings.quote: She sets out the dispute without taking a side of her own.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: counsel's case — the piece is reported journalism; nearly every judgment is attributed (“Askerholt’s reading is narrower”, “he wrote in a trade journal”, “Askerholt’s group had thought his worry overdone”), so a reader can claim the writer merely relays the dispute and the trial arithmetic. The case dies on the writer's own unattributed verdict sentence — “The five streets are his, fairly won; the twenty-five are not” — plus evaluative authorial voice (“One street failed and taught nobody anything”): ‘fairly won’ is the writer scoring the objection herself, which is exactly key B (right on one point, wrong on the rest). Attractive but beatable.

findings.quote: The boxes were divided mainly because more parishioners wanted seats than the church could hold.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: counsel's case — after division “names crowd where one household's name used to stand”, pew 9 “carries three surnames by 1856”, and “In 1861 the wardens raised the price of the front boxes to a pound” — crowding plus a price rise reads as demand outstripping supply. The case dies on the occupancy data at the moment of the change: “Six pews in the middle aisle are marked vacant that year, and four the year after” immediately precedes “In the plan of 1851 the vacant marks are gone”, and free benches stood at the west door — vacant pews contradict ‘more wanted seats than the church could hold’; the price rise is ten years later. Requires importing later data and ignoring the vacancies; attractive but beatable.

findings.quote: Den bygger på ett enda kvällsbesök i augusti.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: counsel's case — the author really does attack the single August visit (“som stöd redovisas ett besök i augusti då förvaltningen räknade till fyra personer”; “Augustibesöket bevisar inte heller det som tjänsteskrivelsen låter påskina”), so the option states a criticism genuinely made in the text. It dies on the prompt delimiter ‘i kommunens kalkyl’: the text pins kalkylen to the savings figure (“kalkylen i tjänsteskrivelsen anger en besparing på 38 000 kronor”), whose stated flaw is “Kalkylen utgår ändå från de gamla lamporna”; the visit supports the separate ‘begränsat för flertalet motionärer’ claim, so ‘Den [kalkylen] bygger på’ the visit is false as written. Strongest distractor in the batch; beatable, but only via the delimiter.

findings.quote: Han antyder att frågan knappast kan besvaras, eftersom minnesbilderna av vem som rodde var kan ha tillrättalagts i efterhand.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: counsel's case — the first clause matches the author's agnosticism (“Jag vet ärligt talat inte vad sätena visade”) and “Misstanken att eftervärlden … läser in mer ordning än roddarna kände av går inte att lägga undan” can be stretched into ‘efterhand-tillrättaläggning’. It dies on the stated reason: his doubt concerns posterity's INTERPRETATION of what the seats meant (“eftervärlden, jag själv inräknad, läser in mer ordning”), while the seating facts themselves are treated as reliable (“Vem som satt var i båten var ingen tillfällighet: varje gård i båtlaget hade sin toft”) — he never suggests doctored recollections of who rowed where. Attractive near-miss; beatable.
